content: The Stoics identified four primary passions, which were defined in detail by Andronicus in his work On Passions. These definitions were later translated and modified by Long and Sedley. The Stoics also recognized numerous subdivisions within these primary passions, as further elaborated in Cicero's Tusculan Disputations, translated by J.E. King. The four primary passions are: 1. Distress 2. Fear 3. Lust 4. Delight In 1980, Robert Plutchik developed a model known as the wheel of emotions, which categorized emotions into eight basic emotions and eight advanced emotions. The advanced emotions were combinations of two basic emotions. The artificial language Lojban includes a system of interjections that express various degrees of emotions. These emotions are categorized as follows: Simple Emotions: Discovery versus confusion Gain versus loss Generosity versus greed Surprise versus no surprise versus expectation Wonder versus commonplace Happiness versus unhappiness Amusement versus weariness Completion versus incompleteness Courage versus timidity versus cowardice Pity versus cruelty Repentance versus lack of regret versus innocence Complex Emotions: Fear versus nervousness versus security Togetherness versus privacy Respect versus disrespect Appreciation versus envy Love versus indifference versus hatred Familiarity versus mystery Propositional Attitudes: Attentive versus inattentive versus avoiding Alertness versus exhaustion Intent versus indecision versus refusal Effort versus no real effort versus repose Hope versus despair Desire versus indifference versus reluctance Interest versus no interest versus repulsion Complex Propositional Attitudes: Permission versus prohibition Competence versus incompetence Obligation versus freedom Constraint versus independence versus resistance to constraint Request versus negative request Suggestion versus no suggestion versus warning Understanding versus confusion
